newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay suspends A330-300 operations.
newsitem.headline: Cathay suspends A330-300 operations.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Saturday it had suspended operations of its 11 Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft due to concerns about the reliability of their Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.

"Cathay Pacific has chosen to take the precautionary measure of suspending A330-300 operations until the engine manufacturer can provide sufficient assurance that the reliability problems of the engine are resolved," the company said in a statement.

Cathay said the decision followed the failure of a Trent 700 engine on a Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) A330 on Friday. Flight KA-MH061 from Hong Kong made an emergency landing at Subic Bay in the Philippines on Friday after developing engine trouble en route to Kota Kinabalu in Malaysia.

"The failure occurred on a brand new component of the engine and the possibility of some form of assembly or quality problem cannot be ruled out until a full inspection has taken place," Cathay Pacific said.
Dragonair also said later it had suspended operations of its A330-300 fleet of four aircraft.

Problems in the Trent 700 engines have forced a series of unscheduled single-engine landings recently. Cathay Pacific said the problem with an engine part in the Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engine had been "clearly identified and understood" and a long-term design solution had been found.

"However, as standard procedure, this design will have to be endurance tested before it can be released for service," it said. "As a result, Cathay Pacific has decided to avoid exposing its passengers and staff to any level of risk however small."
Cathay Pacific said the suspension, with immediate effect, did not affect any of its other aircraft fleets or engine types.
The Hong Kong carrier is about 44 percent owned by Swire Pacific Ltd.
Swire Pacific and Cathay Pacific together hold about 26 percent of Dragonair. Dragonair's major shareholder is China National Aviation Corp.
